M1_Strict_Right_Circular_Cylinder_6DOF.description: Strict cylinder with s=1.000 fixed, collinear centers, dorsal edge tangent at r_dor = a

M2_Cylinder_Free_Dorsal_Crest_Offset_7DO.description: Strict cylinder with s=1.000 fixed, collinear centers, free dorsal crest offset r_dor

M3_Equal_Weight_Compromise_Cylinder_6DOF.description: Cylinder-compatible equal-diameter front/rear ellipses, collinear projected centers, and freely fitted dorsal offset; axis selected by unweighted scan (7 effective parameters)

M4_Tapered_Conical_Frustum_Coupled_8DOF.description: Tapered cone with floating scale ratio s and coupled dorsal silhouette tilt alpha

competing_tapered_model_m4.mechanism: In the coupled joint model M4, the optimizer drives s to 0.619 because the resulting 9.46° taper angle alpha couples the body axis (39.33°) to the observed dorsal silhouette edge (29.86° vs 28.89° measured), while shifting the collinear rear center to accommodate a smaller rear cap.

standalone_rear_arc_curvature.conclusion: The 24-point exposed rear arc curvature alone does NOT prefer an extreme 0.619 taper (at s=0.60, rear RMS degrades to 0.272 px). The rear arc alone is mathematically underdetermined across s in [0.85, 1.15] (Delta_RMS < 0.013 px) and is fully consistent with an unscaled cylinder cap (s = 1.000, Delta_RMS = 0.0017 px).

scale_ratio_analysis.reconciliation_verdict: The apparent contradiction between the prose ('taper is unconstrained around 1.0') and the M4 optimization (s = 0.619, RMS = 0.255 px) arises from conflating two different geometric formulations. Standalone rear-arc curvature cannot discriminate taper (Delta_RMS < 0.013 px across [0.85, 1.15]), whereas the coupled joint model M4 couples the dorsal silhouette angle to the body axis via alpha(s), driving s to 0.619 to reconcile the 3.8° angular spread. Crucially, the strict cylinder fits (Model 1 at 0.3788 px RMS and Model 2 at 0.3468 px RMS) remain genuine, subpixel matches across all 85 points without requiring any physical taper.
scale_ratio_analysis.conclusion: Standalone rear-arc curvature is consistent with a cylinder (s = 1.000, Delta_RMS < 0.002 px wrt minimum), while the coupled joint model M4 optimizes to s = 0.619 (95% CI [0.61, 0.63]) by using a 9.46° taper angle to bridge the axis-dorsal angular spread.

1_ellipse_orientation_unidentifiability.verdict: Fully explained by observational noise (0.67 sigma, p = 0.50). The front rim has b/a = 0.83 over an incomplete 175° arc, making its orientation unidentifiable to within ±4.2°.

2_baseline_lever_arm_sensitivity.verdict: A transverse shift of the rear center by only 1.1 px rotates the center-to-center bearing by 1.6°. Over a 24-px single-side arc, centroid uncertainty alone explains the bearing difference.

3_camera_perspective_convergence.verdict: Central perspective convergence is only ~0.13°, an order of magnitude too small to explain the 3.3° spread alone.

4_physical_conical_taper.verdict: In Model 4, a taper ratio s = 0.619 (half-angle alpha = 9.46°) couples the body axis (39.33°) to the dorsal silhouette edge (29.86°), matching the measured edge (28.89°) to within 0.97° and achieving 0.2549 px total RMS.

5_joint_compromise_axis.verdict: A shared projected cylinder axis with a free dorsal offset provides subpixel fits. This is a seven-parameter cylinder-compatible image model, not the outer-silhouette-tangent constraint of Model 1.
